title: Console history
description:
Build `History`, the command history behind Delve's console, with the behaviour of a typical terminal.

- `submit(line)` records a submitted command (empty lines and a line identical to the most recent entry are not recorded), and resets browsing.
- `up(current)` is called when Up is pressed, with the text currently in the input line. The first press saves `current` as the **draft** and returns the most recent command; each further press returns an older one, stopping at the oldest (pressing Up there returns the oldest again). With no history, it returns `current` unchanged.
- `down()` moves to a newer entry. Moving past the newest returns the saved draft, and browsing ends. If not browsing, it returns the draft (initially empty).
- The history keeps at most `capacity` entries (given to the constructor), dropping the oldest.

```
submit "give potion 5", submit "heal"
up("go")   -> "heal"
up("...")  -> "give potion 5"
up("...")  -> "give potion 5"        (the oldest; stays)
down()     -> "heal"
down()     -> "go"                   (the draft is back)
```
hints: Keep a flag for "browsing", the index of the entry being shown, and the draft. The first Up starts browsing at the newest entry and saves the draft; later Ups move the index down, but not below 0.
Down moves the index up; when there is no newer entry, browsing ends and the draft is returned.
